home.title: Zigbee, bridged to Matter.
home.lead: Connect Zigbee devices to Matter ecosystems without an MQTT broker.
home.intro: Built on Zigbee2MQTT’s device, coordinator and converter ecosystem, Zigbee2Matter exposes supported capabilities through a Matter bridge.
cards: Choose Home Assistant OS, Docker or source installation, then connect your coordinator and first device.
Search the Zigbee converter catalogue and learn what device support means for Matter.
Set up the coordinator, frontend, API, Zigbee network and Matter bridge.
home.architectureTitle: Zigbee state in, Matter endpoints out
home.architecture: The Zigbee network remains the source of device state. Supported capabilities are mapped to persistent Matter endpoints, with optional Home Assistant and REST/WebSocket interfaces.
home.architectureAlt: Diagram showing Zigbee devices connected through Zigbee2Matter to Matter, Home Assistant and API clients
home.project: Zigbee2Matter is not an official Zigbee2MQTT or Connectivity Standards Alliance product. Zigbee converter support does not guarantee that every feature maps to Matter.

guide.title: Install and connect your first device
guide.lead: Choose a platform, configure the Zigbee coordinator, then pair and check a device.
sections:
• A supported Zigbee coordinator connected by USB or TCP.
  • For source installs: Linux, Node.js 22.13.x or 24.x, and pnpm 11.26.
  • For Matter: IPv6 and mDNS multicast between the bridge and controller on the same local network.
  • Persistent storage for configuration, Zigbee network data and Matter fabric keys.

Keep the coordinator away from USB 3 and Wi-Fi interference. Make a separate backup before migrating an existing network.

Add the Zigbee2Matter repository to Home Assistant

  1. Open the pre-filled repository dialog and select Add.
  2. Close the dialog, refresh the app store if needed, and install Zigbee2Matter.
  3. Open the app configuration, set the coordinator serial port and adapter, then start it. Use the app's Home Assistant sidebar entry to open the frontend.

Host networking is enabled for Matter mDNS and UDP 5540. Configuration and Zigbee data are stored under /data and included in Home Assistant backups. Docker and source installs use the platform-specific steps below.

From the repository root, set the variables for your coordinator and start one Compose profile. Host networking is used for coordinator access and Matter discovery.

# USB coordinator
export ZIGBEE2MATTER_USB_DEVICE=/dev/serial/by-id/your-coordinator
docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml --profile usb up -d --build

# TCP coordinator
export ZIGBEE2MATTER_SERIAL_PORT=tcp://192.168.1.20:6638
export ZIGBEE2MATTER_SERIAL_ADAPTER=ember
docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml --profile tcp up -d --build

The frontend listens on port 8080. Restrict access with your firewall. Keep the named zigbee2matter-data volume when updating the container.

Use Node.js 22.13.x or 24.x and pnpm 11.26 in the repository root.

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run build
pnpm start

The default frontend is http://localhost:8080. Runtime files are stored in the configured data directory.

1. Open the frontend and check startup logs for coordinator errors.
  2. If discovery fails, set serial.port and serial.adapter in configuration.yaml. The default source path is data/configuration.yaml; HAOS uses /data/configuration.yaml, and Docker Compose uses /app/data/configuration.yaml.
  3. Use a stable /dev/serial/by-id/... USB path or tcp://host:port. Stop the service before editing configuration, then restart it.
  4. Confirm the bridge is online before enabling Matter or migrating automations.

Common adapter values include zstack, ember, deconz, zigate and zboss.

1. Temporarily enable permit-join in the frontend.
  2. Put the device into pairing mode using its manufacturer instructions, near the coordinator.
  3. Wait for the interview to finish and confirm the model and support status.
  4. Assign a friendly name and try its controls in the frontend.
  5. Disable permit-join when finished.

A device may join Zigbee even when its controls or Matter mapping are unsupported. Search the device catalogue for pairing notes.

configuration.title: Configuration reference
configuration.lead: Configuration is read from the runtime data directory. Stop the service before editing the file, then restart to apply changes.
sections:
Set these only when automatic discovery does not find the adapter or when the connection needs an explicit path.

serial:
  port: /dev/serial/by-id/your-coordinator
  adapter: ember

For a network coordinator, use tcp://host:port. Common adapter values are zstack, ember, deconz, zigate and zboss.

The web frontend is enabled by default on port 8080.

frontend:
  enabled: true
  port: 8080

When binding it to a LAN address, limit access to trusted devices with a firewall.

The API defaults to loopback on port 8090. Configure an authentication token before exposing it beyond localhost.

api:
  enabled: true
  host: 127.0.0.1
  port: 8090
  # auth_token: !secret zigbee2matter_api_token

Keep the data directory persistent. It contains the Zigbee database and network identity. The example configuration generates network keys and IDs on first start; do not replace these values when restoring an existing network.

advanced:
  network_key: GENERATE
  pan_id: GENERATE
  ext_pan_id: GENERATE

Start with Matter disabled. For commissioning, enable the bridge and set both commissioning values together. IPv6 is required; mDNS must pass between the bridge and controller on the same local network.

matter:
  enabled: true
  passcode: 20202021
  discriminator: 3840
  attestation:
    mode: development

Development attestation is for development use. Production use needs owner-provided credentials and VID authorization. Never share passcodes, private keys or fabric backups.
See the complete example configuration in the source repository.
